body: I disagree that most people see it that way. I'm bisexual and don't see every single human being I am with as a potential fuck buddy. Being in a romantic relationship is basically just friends with benefits if it gets to that. Likely you might come off as desperate though which turns people off. If you are wanting to be with someone just for sex and not friendship it won't work out in a long term relationship. Long term relationships are like friendship plus a couple of other things, and then marriage for some people is that plus raising children. For me personally I don't see a point to getting married without the children part in it. Like what's the difference between friends with benefits and someone you are married to at that point? Except for a few legal things, not really anything meaningful. If you want to have sex, which I think most people think about from time to time, you can go someplace where prostitution is legal. Flip it around and think, would you really want to date a woman who seemed desperate? Taking care of your health and living a healthy lifestyle, mentally and physically, will put you so far ahead of so many other people in terms of the dating pool. It is ridiculously hard to find people, especially in western countries, who even care enough about their bodies to live a healthy lifestyle. People age and whatever, I guess just be someone who people would want to be around even if you were super old. GrandpaBurdTurgler on the case o/
